blueprint_topic: Management of Care — clinical-trial SAE recognition, documentation, protocol adherence, and research-team coordination
stem: A client enrolled in an oncology investigational-drug trial calls the research nurse to report a new adverse event that resulted in an unplanned inpatient hospitalization. Which action best reflects the oncology clinical research nurse's role?

options.A: Assess and document the event, immediately alert the investigator/study team with available information, follow the protocol SAE pathway, and coordinate needed care.
options.B: Assess the client and wait to notify the research team until causality is established because sponsor reporting depends on whether the study drug caused the event.
options.C: Document the hospitalization as an expected toxicity and submit it at the next scheduled safety review when the event is already listed in the protocol or brochure.
options.D: Wait for the discharge diagnosis and complete hospital record before the initial study report, then send the sponsor a single fully characterized event summary.

rationale: A is correct. ONS describes oncology clinical research nursing as requiring precise protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring and reporting, detailed documentation, clinical judgment, and coordination of care. FDA's December 2025 final guidance incorporates the 21 CFR 312.32(a) definition of a serious adverse event and explicitly lists inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of hospitalization among the serious outcomes. Under 21 CFR 312.64(b), the investigator must immediately report any serious adverse event to the sponsor whether or not it is considered drug-related, including events already listed in the protocol or investigator brochure; additional information may be collected and submitted after the initial report. Therefore, the research nurse should assess/document the event, promptly engage the investigator/study team according to the protocol-defined SAE pathway, and coordinate clinically necessary care. B is incorrect because immediate SAE reporting does not wait for causality to be established. C is incorrect because an SAE is not deferred to routine review merely because it is expected or already described in study documents. D is incorrect because FDA permits additional data to follow the initial report rather than requiring a complete discharge record before the first safety communication.
educational_objective: When a clinical-trial participant experiences an adverse event resulting in unplanned inpatient hospitalization, recognize the event as meeting an FDA serious-adverse-event criterion, document and escalate it promptly through the protocol-defined safety pathway, and coordinate needed clinical care without waiting for causality or a complete discharge record.
source_organization: Oncology Nursing Society (ONS); U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
source_document_title: Ready to Manage Clinical Trials? Here's How to Grow Your Competence From Novice to Expert; Investigator Responsibilities — Safety Reporting for Investigational Drugs and Devices
source_version_date: ONS article published January 15, 2026; FDA final guidance issued December 2025 and confirmed in FDA FY2026 reporting; sources rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: ONS January 15, 2026 article, body paragraphs under the CRN competency discussion: oncology trials require precise protocol adherence, complex adverse-event monitoring/reporting, detailed and rigorous documentation, and coordination of care; competency domains include patient safety, trial coordination, regulatory knowledge, data integrity, communication, and clinical judgment. FDA December 2025 final guidance — Definitions, PDF page 7/file page 8: under 21 CFR 312.32(a), an adverse event is serious when it results in outcomes including inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization. Section V.A, PDF page 8/file page 9: under §312.64(b), investigator must immediately report any SAE to sponsor whether or not considered drug-related, including events listed in the protocol or investigator brochure. Section V.B, PDF page 9/file page 10: immediate reporting occurs as soon as feasible after SAE recognition/relevant initial information and more data may be submitted after the initial report.
source_claim_supported: Current ONS guidance supports protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring/reporting, rigorous documentation, clinical judgment, and care coordination as core oncology CRN functions. Current FDA guidance identifies inpatient hospitalization as an SAE criterion and requires immediate investigator-to-sponsor reporting of any SAE regardless of causality or whether the event was already listed, with follow-up information permitted after the initial report.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Client Rights/Safety, Continuity of Care, Concepts of Management, and legal/organizational standards: assess and communicate significant findings, coordinate care with appropriate team members, follow organizational/protocol requirements, document care accurately, and protect client safety within nursing scope.
pdf_visual_verification: FDA December 2025 final guidance PDF page 7/file page 8 was visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20 and visibly showed inpatient hospitalization/prolongation of hospitalization in the serious-adverse-event definition. FDA PDF page 8/file page 9 was visually verified and showed that any SAE must be immediately reported to the sponsor whether or not drug-related, including events listed in the protocol/investigator brochure. FDA PDF page 9/file page 10 was visually verified and showed the timing section and that additional data may follow the initial report. The ONS evidence is current HTML. Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care content had been visually verified earlier in this audit session.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'oncology investigational drug adverse event research nurse protocol investigator severe symptom documentation reporting' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Initial rebuild removed longest-key and cartoon distractors but adversarial reread identified a regulatory ambiguity: a clinically 'severe' symptom is not automatically an FDA 'serious' adverse event. The stem was therefore rebuilt around unplanned inpatient hospitalization, an explicit SAE criterion. Final distractors now test realistic regulatory errors: waiting for causality before reporting, delaying an expected SAE to routine review, and waiting for complete hospital records before the initial safety report.

option_audit.A: Correct; integrates ONS-supported CRN assessment/documentation/coordination with the FDA's immediate SAE reporting framework and protocol-defined safety workflow.
option_audit.B: Plausible causality-first error; incorrect because §312.64(b) requires immediate reporting of any SAE whether or not considered drug-related.
option_audit.C: Plausible expected-event error; incorrect because events listed in the protocol or investigator brochure are still immediately reportable when they meet SAE criteria.
option_audit.D: Plausible complete-information-first error; incorrect because FDA states additional data may be collected/submitted after the initial SAE report.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type distractor absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths are closely balanced (A 165, B 163, C 164, D 160 characters); the key is not identifiable by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel research-safety responses to the same confirmed SAE scenario.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after replacing severity ambiguity with an explicit SAE criterion and re-auditing against current ONS/FDA sources.
